460	/// a preset means the same thing on a 4K canvas as on a vertical one: a size
461	/// of the canvas's SHORT side, a position of its width and height (spec §11
462	/// VR-41), so a tall canvas gets the line height a wide one has.
463	struct TextPreset {
464	    let name: String
465	    let font: String
466	    let sizeFraction: Double
467	    let xFraction: Double
468	    let yFraction: Double
469	    let align: String
470	    let backdrop: BackdropProps?
471	    /// Of H, on a canvas taller than wide, in place of `yFraction` (the Caption
472	    /// row's 0.25, VR-41); nil keeps `yFraction` on every canvas.
473	    var tallYFraction: Double? = nil
474	
475	    /// The font size on `canvas`: `sizeFraction` of `min(W, H)`. On a canvas at
476	    /// least as wide as tall that is H, so the old `H × sizeFraction` is kept to the bit.
477	    func size(on canvas: CGSize) -> Double {
478	        (sizeFraction * Double(min(canvas.width, canvas.height))).rounded()
479	    }
480	
481	    /// Where the box's centre sits on `canvas`.
482	    func position(on canvas: CGSize) -> (x: Double, y: Double) {
483	        let y = canvas.height > canvas.width ? tallYFraction ?? yFraction : yFraction
484	        return (xFraction * Double(canvas.width), y * Double(canvas.height))
485	    }

487	    /// Text ▸ Presets' two patches: the face, size, alignment and backdrop, and where the
488	    /// box sits at full opacity.

492	            TextPatch(

494	                backdrop: .some(backdrop)),

497	    }

520	/// The model's one font string ↔ the panel's family + style pair.
521	///
522	/// Everything here tolerates a name this machine has no font for: a project
523	/// carries PostScript names, and the Text tab still has to open (and still has
524	/// to be able to change the face) on a machine missing that family.
525	enum TextFace {
526	    /// Installed families, sorted. Read once — `availableFontFamilies` walks
527	    /// the font registry, and this popup is rebuilt on every selection change.
528	    static let families: [String] = NSFontManager.shared.availableFontFamilies.sorted()
529	
530	    /// One member of a family: its PostScript name and the style label.
531	    struct Member {
532	        let name: String
533	        let style: String
534	    }
535	
536	    static func members(of family: String) -> [Member] {
537	        let raw = NSFontManager.shared.availableMembers(ofFontFamily: family) ?? []
538	        return raw.compactMap { entry in
539	            guard entry.count >= 2, let name = entry[0] as? String,
540	                  let style = entry[1] as? String
541	            else { return nil }
542	            return Member(name: name, style: style)
543	        }
544	    }
545	
546	    /// The family a stored PostScript name belongs to; the first installed
547	    /// family when the font is missing, so the popup always has a row.
548	    static func family(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
549	        if let font = NSFont(name: postScriptName, size: 12), let family = font.familyName {
550	            return family
551	        }
552	        return families.first ?? "Helvetica"
553	    }
554	
555	    /// The style label of a stored name ("SemiBold"), or "Regular".
556	    static func style(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
557	        let family = family(of: postScriptName)
558	        return members(of: family).first { $0.name == postScriptName }?.style ?? "Regular"
559	    }
560	
561	    /// The PostScript name for a family plus a style label, keeping the style
562	    /// across a family change when the new family has one by that name.
563	    static func postScriptName(family: String, style: String) -> String {
564	        let list = members(of: family)
565	        if let match = list.first(where: { $0.style == style }) { return match.name }
566	        if let regular = list.first(where: { $0.style == "Regular" }) { return regular.name }
567	        return list.first?.name ?? family
568	    }
569	}

1	//! The text vocabulary — [`TextProps`], the [`TextAlign`] and
2	//! [`TextVAlign`] it is placed by, the optional [`Outline`] and
3	//! [`Backdrop`] drawn with it, and the [`TextAnimation`] (with its
4	//! [`TextAnimationKind`]) that reveals it (spec §5.2, §5.3). Version 9's
5	//! three word-caption fields — `case`, `words` and `word_style` — close
6	//! [`TextProps`]; their TYPES are `model_words.rs`'s.
7	//!
8	//! Split out of `model_props.rs` under the size rule (core/CLAUDE.md: a
9	//! module over ~600 lines gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on)
10	//! when road map 2's phase 6 came to add `video.blend` and
11	//! `shape.gradient` to a file already standing at 592. `model.rs` →
12	//! `model_query.rs` in phase 0, `model.rs` → `model_props.rs` in phase 2
13	//! and `model_props.rs` → `model_regions.rs` in phase 3c are the
14	//! precedent, and so is their rule: the cut goes along a seam somebody can
15	//! NAME, and the piece taken out is re-exported whole so not one path
16	//! anywhere else changes. This is also the seam core/CLAUDE.md and the
17	//! road map both named in advance, which is the other half of why it is
18	//! the one phase 6 takes rather than a convenient two hundred lines.
19	//!
20	//! # The seam: the one group the model cannot measure
21	//!
22	//! Every other property group is made of quantities the core owns. A
23	//! `scale`, a `crop`, a shape's `width` and `height`, a region's box: the
24	//! core bounds them (`props_check.rs`), interpolates them (`actions.rs`),
25	//! solves geometry against them (`edit_zoom.rs`) and hands the renderer
26	//! numbers that are already the answer. Text is the one group where the
27	//! model can only state an INTENT — these words, that font, that size —
28	//! because only the platform can lay a string out, and the measurement
29	//! comes back the other way, through a cache the renderer fills (spec
30	//! §5.3, §11). Nothing here is ever a measured size, and that is a
31	//! standing rule rather than an omission.
32	//!
33	//! The rest of the file follows from it. `align`, `valign`,
34	//! `line_spacing`, `tracking`, `width`, the outline and the backdrop are
35	//! all instructions to that one layout and are meaningless to anything
36	//! that is not performing it; and [`TextAnimation`] is the same fact one
37	//! step further on — the model says WHAT the reveal is, `recipe.rs`'s
38	//! `Reveal` turns it into one number per frame, and the platform is the
39	//! only thing that knows which glyphs, words or lines that number picks
40	//! out. A file of types nothing but a text layout engine can consume is
41	//! one concern.
42	//!
43	//! What is NOT here: the field that HOLDS these values — `Clip.text` —
44	//! which is part of the clip's own shape and stays in `model.rs` with it;
45	//! the per-frame reveal the animation becomes, which `recipe.rs` computes
46	//! and never stores; and the caption machinery that produces text clips
47	//! (`CaptionCues`, `CaptionLayout`), which is Swift and is placement, not
48	//! schema.
49	//!
50	//! # Paths
51	//!
52	//! `model_props.rs` re-exports this module whole with
53	//! `pub use crate::model_text::*`, and `model.rs` re-exports
54	//! `model_props.rs` the same way, so `crate::model_props::TextProps`,
55	//! `crate::model::TextProps` and the crate-root re-exports in `lib.rs` all
56	//! still resolve and no other file needed an import changed. The schema
57	//! rules are `model.rs`'s too: the field names ARE the JSON keys,
58	//! declaration order IS key order, every type is `#[serde(default)]` over a
59	//! hand-written [`Default`] that says what an absent key means, and nothing
60	//! here carries `deny_unknown_fields`.

178	/// How a text layer arrives and how it leaves (format version 5, road map
179	/// 2's phase 4c).
180	///
181	/// Three keys and no fourth. `in` and `out` are DURATIONS, not times: the
182	/// reveal runs for `in` from the clip's own first frame, and the un-reveal
183	/// for `out` back from its own last one — the clip's, never the instance's,
184	/// which is the rule `recipe.rs` already states for clip time, so a nest
185	/// clip's edge cuts a nested caption off mid-reveal rather than making it
186	/// un-reveal early. Either may be 0, meaning that end of the animation
187	/// simply does not happen.
188	///
189	/// There is deliberately no curve field. The shape of the motion is
190	/// already in the kind — a typewriter's step per character, a word fade's
191	/// stagger, a line rise's per-line offset — and easing between two
192	/// arbitrary values is what the action system is for (spec §5.4). A curve
193	/// can be added later as a defaulted fourth key with no migration step,
194	/// which is the test this crate applies to leaving a field out.
195	///
196	/// Nothing here is a measurement of pixels or of time inside the reveal:
197	/// the model says what the animation IS, `recipe.rs` turns it into one
198	/// number per frame, and the platform draws it (spec §7). That is also why
199	/// the discriminant is called `kind` and not, say, `style`:
200	/// `actions.rs`'s object rule holds two objects that both name a DIFFERING
201	/// `kind` until the interpolation is over, so an action that moves a clip
202	/// from a typewriter to a line rise switches at the end instead of
203	/// interpolating an `in` between two animations that do not measure the
204	/// same thing.
205	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
206	#[serde(default)]
207	pub struct TextAnimation {
208	    pub kind: TextAnimationKind,
209	    /// How long the reveal takes, from the clip's first frame.
210	    #[serde(rename = "in")]
211	    pub r#in: Ticks,
212	    /// How long the un-reveal takes, measured back from the clip's last
213	    /// frame.
214	    pub out: Ticks,
215	}
216	
217	impl Default for TextAnimation {
218	    /// A one-second typewriter that does not un-reveal — the animation a
219	    /// user gets for switching the section on and saying nothing else.
220	    ///
221	    /// The kind is the typewriter for the reason
222	    /// [`crate::model::Filter::default`] gives: a default has to be visibly
223	    /// SOMETHING the moment it is turned on, or the control reads as
224	    /// broken, and of the three this is the one everybody can already name
225	    /// before they see it. One second is that same test applied to the
226	    /// duration — long enough to read as typing rather than as a cut, short
227	    /// enough that a three-second caption is not still arriving when it is
228	    /// due to leave.
229	    ///

233	    /// animated title would be a surprise rather than a convenience.

243	/// The three reveals of spec §4.3, closed at three.
244	///
245	/// Closed for [`crate::model::ObscureKind`]'s reason: each one is a
246	/// distinct drawing routine in `LayerRenderers.renderText`, not a shared
247	/// one — a prefix of the glyphs, a per-word alpha ramp, a per-line offset
248	/// and alpha — so an unknown kind is a value nothing downstream could
249	/// repair, and there is no neutral animation to fall back to the way a
250	/// filter's `amount` can fall back to 0. Refusing it at the serde boundary
251	/// makes the illegal state unrepresentable.

254	/// declaration order here — the recipe carries the kind by NAME, unlike
255	/// [`crate::model::ObscureKind`], whose order is a shader discriminant —
256	/// but the JSON spelling of each variant is persisted, so it may not be
257	/// renamed without a migration step.
258	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
259	#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
260	pub enum TextAnimationKind {
261	    /// The default, and [`TextAnimation::default`] says why: the one
262	    /// reveal a user can name before they have seen it.
263	    #[default]
264	    Typewriter,
265	    WordFade,
266	    LineRise,
267	}

161	    /// The gradient fill (§5.2's `shape.gradient`, format version 6): a
162	    /// geometry, an angle and the stops, all of it one `set_shape` patch.
163	    ///
164	    /// Three rules out of the schema show up here as UI, and none of them is
165	    /// this file's invention:
166	    ///
167	    ///  - **Every write sends the WHOLE object.** The core MERGES a nested
168	    ///    object into a stored one key by key (§5.2), but a stored `null` is
169	    ///    not an object: `actions::merge` replaces it with what the patch
170	    ///    carries, and the keys left out then come from `Gradient::default()`
171	    ///    rather than from what the clip had. This section is where a
172	    ///    gradient is turned ON from null, so it sends every key and is right
173	    ///    in both cases. `shadow` has carried that since M3 and `obscure`
174	    ///    since phase 3; `edited` below is where `gradient` joins them.
175	    ///  - **The Fill rows above stay live.** A gradient takes precedence over
176	    ///    `fill` and does not clear it, which is what makes this section's
177	    ///    Reset — one `{gradient: null}` — an exact inverse rather than a
178	    ///    shape that goes invisible. Disabling the colour underneath would
179	    ///    hide the value the Reset is about to bring back, so the note says
180	    ///    where the fill went instead of the panel pretending it is gone.
181	    ///  - **`line` and `arrow` get the rows DISABLED, not hidden.** The field
182	    ///    is stored and range-checked on every kind and read by the two area
183	    ///    kinds alone — `radius`'s precedent exactly — so flipping the Kind
184	    ///    popup to Line and back may not lose the ramp.
185	    func gradientSection() -> InspectorSection {
186	        let binding = self.binding
187	        let kinds = GradientKind.allCases
188	        func current() -> Gradient? { binding.shapeProps.gradient }
189	        func on() -> Bool { current() != nil }
190	        /// Whether this kind has an interior to fill at all.
191	        func area() -> Bool { !binding.shapeProps.kind.isLinear }
192	        func list() -> [GradientStop] { current()?.stops ?? [] }
193	        func at(_ index: Int) -> GradientStop? {
194	            let stops = list()
195	            return stops.indices.contains(index) ? stops[index] : nil
196	        }
197	        func ops(_ next: Gradient?) -> [ReelOp] {
198	            binding.ops(shape: ShapePatch(gradient: .some(next)))
199	        }
200	        /// The gradient with `change` applied and the other keys as they
201	        /// stand. This is the "send it whole" rule above, spelled once so that
202	        /// no row has to remember it.
203	        func edited(_ change: (inout Gradient) -> Void) -> [ReelOp] {
204	            guard var gradient = current() else { return [] }
205	            change(&gradient)
206	            return ops(gradient)
207	        }
208	        func edited(replacing index: Int, _ stop: GradientStop) -> [ReelOp] {
209	            var next = list()
210	            guard next.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
211	            next[index] = stop
212	            return edited { $0.stops = next }
213	        }
214	        /// The mixed badge for one stop's field: a selection where some clip
215	        /// has no gradient, or none at that index, disagrees — which the
216	        /// `nil` says, the way `obscureSection`'s `mixedAt` says it.
217	        func mixedAt<T: Equatable>(_ index: Int, _ read: @escaping (GradientStop) -> T) -> Bool {
218	            binding.mixedShape { props -> T? in
219	                guard let stops = props.gradient?.stops, stops.indices.contains(index)
220	                else { return nil }
221	                return read(stops[index])
222	            }
223	        }
224	        /// The colour half way between two stops, component by component —
225	        /// which is exactly what `CGGradient` does between them, in the same
226	        /// sRGB space, so a handle added here sits ON the ramp rather than
227	        /// beside it. A three-component colour is an opaque one (`RGBA`'s own
228	        /// rule), so both are padded the same way before they are mixed.
229	        func midpoint(_ a: RGBA, _ b: RGBA) -> RGBA {
230	            func component(_ color: RGBA, _ index: Int) -> Double {
231	                index < color.count ? color[index] : (index == 3 ? 1 : 0)
232	            }
233	            return (0..<4).map { (component(a, $0) + component(b, $0)) / 2 }
234	        }
235	        /// A stop dropped into the WIDEST gap and coloured by the ramp that
236	        /// is already there, so Add changes the picture not at all: it puts a
237	        /// handle where the ramp already runs, which is what Add means in
238	        /// every gradient editor. The model cannot do this for you —
239	        /// `GradientStop`'s own default is black at 0, because serde has to
240	        /// fill a missing key without knowing which row was clicked.
241	        ///
242	        /// It inserts into the list as it is HELD, never into the sorted one.
243	        /// The rows are drawn in held order and the core deliberately does
244	        /// not police that order (`props_check.rs` argues the missing check
245	        /// where it would have gone), so sorting here would make every row
246	        /// jump the first time somebody pressed Add.
247	        func added(_ stops: [GradientStop]) -> [GradientStop] {
248	            guard stops.count >= 2 else { return Gradient.defaultStops }
249	            let ramp = stops.enumerated().sorted {
250	                $0.element.at == $1.element.at
251	                    ? $0.offset < $1.offset : $0.element.at < $1.element.at
252	            }
253	            var widest = -1.0
254	            var left = ramp[0]
255	            var right = ramp[1]
256	            for (a, b) in zip(ramp, ramp.dropFirst()) where b.element.at - a.element.at > widest {
257	                widest = b.element.at - a.element.at
258	                left = a
259	                right = b
260	            }
261	            var next = stops
262	            next.insert(
263	                GradientStop(
264	                    at: (left.element.at + right.element.at) / 2,
265	                    color: midpoint(left.element.color, right.element.color)),
266	                at: left.offset + 1)
267	            return next
268	        }
269	
270	        var rows: [NSView] = [
271	            inspectorCheckRow(
272	                "Gradient", binding, name: "Gradient", read: on,
273	                ops: { value in ops(value ? Gradient() : nil) },
274	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient != nil } },
275	                enabled: area),
276	            inspectorPopupRow(
277	                "Kind", binding, name: "Gradient Kind", items: kinds.map { $0.displayName },
278	                read: { kinds.firstIndex(of: current()?.kind ?? .linear) ?? 0 },
279	                ops: { index in
280	                    guard kinds.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
281	                    return edited { $0.kind = kinds[index] }
282	                },
283	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient?.kind } },
284	                enabled: { on() && area() }),
285	            // Degrees from the RIGHT, counter-clockwise, and the same eight
286	            // quick picks the shadow's angle gets, because it is the same
287	            // convention and the crate has only the one.
288	            inspectorValueRow(
289	                "Angle", binding, name: "Gradient Angle", unit: "°", decimals: 0, min: 0,
290	                max: 360, quick: [0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315],
291	                read: { current()?.angle ?? 0 },
292	                ops: { v in edited { $0.angle = v } },
293	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient?.angle } },
294	                // A radial gradient has no direction to point: the model
295	                // stores the angle through the flip all the same, so coming
296	                // back to Linear finds the number where it was left.
297	                enabled: { on() && area() && current()?.kind == .linear }),
298	        ]
299	        for index in 0..<list().count {
300	            let swatch = OptionSwatchControl(
301	                read: { at(index)?.color.nsColor ?? .black },
302	                write: { color in
303	                    guard let stop = at(index),
304	                        let next = changedRGBA(color, from: stop.color)
305	                    else { return }
306	                    binding.apply(
307	                        "Gradient Stop",
308	                        edited(replacing: index, GradientStop(at: stop.at, color: next)))
309	                },
310	                enabled: area, onEdit: {})
311	            // A stop's position is 0–1 in the model and a PERCENTAGE here,
312	            // for `video.opacity`'s reason: the ramp is a distance across the
313	            // box, and nobody reads 0.35 of a box as a third of the way.
314	            let position = OptionFieldControl(
315	                width: InspectorMetrics.fieldWidth, unit: "%", decimals: 0, min: 0, max: 100,
316	                quick: [0, 25, 50, 75, 100],
317	                read: { (at(index)?.at ?? 0) * 100 },
318	                write: { value in
319	                    guard let stop = at(index) else { return }
320	                    binding.apply(
321	                        "Gradient Stop",
322	                        edited(replacing: index, GradientStop(at: value / 100, color: stop.color)))
323	                },
324	                enabled: area,
325	                onEdit: { binding.edited() })
326	            let remove = OptionButtonControl(
327	                title: "Remove",
328	                action: {
329	                    var next = list()
330	                    guard next.count > 2, next.indices.contains(index) else {
331	                        NSSound.beep()
332	                        return
333	                    }
334	                    next.remove(at: index)
335	                    binding.apply("Remove Stop", edited { $0.stops = next })
336	                },
337	                enabled: { area() && list().count > 2 }, onEdit: {})
338	            remove.toolTip =
339	                "Take this colour off the ramp — two stops is the floor, because one "
340	                + "colour is a fill and Fill above already spells that"
341	            rows.append(
342	                inspectorRow(
343	                    "Stop \(index + 1)", [swatch, position, remove],
344	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.color } || mixedAt(index) { $0.at } }))
345	        }
346	        if !on() {
347	            rows.append(inspectorRow(nil, [InspectorRowLabel("No gradient.")]))
348	        }
349	        let add = OptionButtonControl(
350	            title: "Add Stop",
351	            action: {
352	                let next = added(list())
353	                guard next.count > list().count else {
354	                    NSSound.beep()
355	                    return
356	                }
357	                binding.apply("Add Stop", edited { $0.stops = next })
358	            },
359	            enabled: { area() && on() && list().count < Gradient.maxStops }, onEdit: {})
360	        add.toolTip =
361	            "Put a handle on the ramp where the ramp already is — the widest gap, "
362	            + "at the colour that is already there"
363	        rows.append(inspectorButtonRow([add, InspectorRowLabel("\(Gradient.maxStops) at most")]))
364	
365	        return InspectorSection(
366	            id: "shape.gradient", title: "Gradient",
367	            summary: {
368	                guard let gradient = current() else { return "off" }
369	                return "\(gradient.kind.displayName.lowercased()), \(gradient.stops.count) stops"
370	            },
371	            note: {
372	                guard area() else {
373	                    return "Fills the rectangle or ellipse; a line or arrow keeps its "
374	                        + "stroke colour."
375	                }
376	                guard on(), binding.shapeProps.fill != nil else { return nil }
377	                return "The gradient covers the Fill colour above; Reset brings it back."
378	            },
379	            reset: { binding.apply("Gradient", shape: ShapePatch(gradient: .some(nil))) },
380	            defaultExpanded: false,
381	            rows: rows)
382	    }

1	//! The shape vocabulary — [`ShapeProps`], the [`ShapeKind`] it draws, the
2	//! [`Stroke`] around it and the [`Gradient`] (with [`GradientKind`],
3	//! [`GradientStop`] and the [`MAX_GRADIENT_STOPS`] budget on it) that fills
4	//! it.
5	//!
6	//! Cut out of `model_props.rs` in road map 5's E2, when that file stood AT
7	//! the 600-line cap owing `video.motion`, and cut HERE because
8	//! `model_text.rs` is its own precedent: a whole property group moved out
9	//! with the types only it names. Text and shape are the two CPU-rendered,
10	//! hash-keyed sources — neither reaches the fragment stage as a sampled
11	//! texture the model describes, both are drawn by
12	//! `LayerRenderers`/`LayerRenderersText` into one, and both are keyed by
13	//! the recipe's content hash — so taking the second after the first leaves
14	//! `model_props.rs` holding what the compositor's uniform block is read
15	//! from and nothing else. Nothing here is ever a shader discriminant, and
16	//! that is a standing rule rather than an omission: [`GradientKind`]'s own
17	//! doc says a kind may be added at the END and that nothing derives a
18	//! number from the order, where [`crate::model::BlendMode`]'s order IS the
19	//! discriminant.
20	//!
21	//! Re-exported whole by `model_props.rs`, which `model.rs` re-exports whole
22	//! in turn, so `crate::model::ShapeProps` and every other path is
23	//! unchanged. The FIELD that holds these values (`Clip.shape`) stays in
24	//! `model.rs` with the clip's other property groups.
25	//!
26	//! The rules are `model.rs`'s: the field names ARE the JSON keys,
27	//! declaration order IS key order, every type is `#[serde(default)]` over a
28	//! hand-written [`Default`] that says what an absent key means, and nothing
29	//! here carries `deny_unknown_fields`.
30	
31	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
32	
33	use crate::model::Color;
34	
35	/// A shape layer. A rounded rectangle is [`ShapeKind::Rectangle`] with a
36	/// non-zero `radius`; `from`/`to` are unit coordinates inside the box and
37	/// apply to lines and arrows only (spec §5.2).
38	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
39	#[serde(default)]
40	pub struct ShapeProps {
41	    pub kind: ShapeKind,
42	    pub width: f64,
43	    pub height: f64,
44	    pub stroke: Option<Stroke>,
45	    pub fill: Option<Color>,
46	    pub arrow_start: bool,
47	    pub arrow_end: bool,
48	    pub radius: f64,
49	    pub from: [f64; 2],
50	    pub to: [f64; 2],
51	    /// A gradient fill, taking precedence over `fill` when set
52	    /// (format version 6). Ignored on `Line` and `Arrow`, which have no
53	    /// area.
54	    pub gradient: Option<Gradient>,
55	}
56	
57	impl Default for ShapeProps {
58	    /// The spec §5.2 example's box, stroked and unfilled so a newly added
59	    /// shape is visible over any footage.
60	    fn default() -> Self {
61	        ShapeProps {
62	            kind: ShapeKind::Rectangle,

227	        GradientStop {
228	            at: 0.0,
229	            color: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is

traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.

  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).

  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

import struct, sys, glob, os

def tables(d):
    n = struct.unpack(">H", d[4:6])[0]
    t = {}
    for i in range(n):
        tag, _, off, ln = struct.unpack(">4sIII", d[12 + i * 16:28 + i * 16])
        t[tag.decode()] = (off, ln)
    return t

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the

content.content:
## Shape clips

Click the timeline bar's **Add Shape** button and pick **Rectangle**,
**Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**. Like text, the shape goes on the front-most
track if there is room, lasts 5 seconds, can be trimmed to any length, and
opens on the **Shape** sub-tab.

A new shape is a 320 × 120 box with a 6 px white stroke and no fill, so it
shows up over any footage. A new arrow has its head at the end turned on. A
new line or arrow runs diagonally across its box. A rounded rectangle is a
Rectangle with a corner radius, not a separate kind.

*Agents:* `add_shape_clip` (track, at, optional duration and shape, either a
kind name or a shape patch); `set_shape` for geometry and paint.

### The Shape tab

| Section | Rows |
|---|---|
| **Shape** | **Kind** (Rectangle, Ellipse, Line, Arrow), **Width** and **Height** 1–20000 px, **Corner radius** 0–2000 px (rectangles only) |
| **Stroke** | **Stroke** on/off, **Width** 0.5–200 px (default 6), **Color** (default white) |
| **Fill** | **Fill** on/off (white when first turned on), **Color**, **Opacity** 0–100 % |
| **Gradient** | Fills the shape with a colour ramp in place of the flat fill (below) |
| **Arrowheads** | **Arrowhead at start**, **Arrowhead at end** (lines and arrows only) |

A shape also gets the Picture tab's Transform, Shadow, Filters, Reflection,
Spotlight and Obscure sections.

### Gradients

Tick **Gradient** to fill a rectangle or ellipse with a colour ramp. A new
gradient is **Linear**, black to white, at 0°.

- **Kind**: **Linear** or **Radial**.
- **Angle**: 0–360°, linear only. 0° runs to the right and the angle turns
  counter-clockwise.

You import an image the same way as a movie (see
[Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)), and it lands as a 5-second clip.
An image has no length of its own, so you can trim it to any duration. Image
clips have everything on the Picture tab, Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key
included, and a Color tab for grading. Remove Background works on a picture too,
keeping its person or its foreground subject (see
[Remove Background](#remove-background)).

- **Video, image, still, graphic and nest clips** have one uniform scale. Every
  handle scales the whole picture and keeps its aspect ratio.
- **Shape clips** change their box size instead. A corner handle keeps the
  aspect ratio and ⇧ frees it. An edge handle changes only the width or only
  the height.
- **Text clips**: the left and right edge handles set the text box's wrap
  width, which makes the box fixed-width. The corners and the top and bottom
  edges scale the text uniformly.

A drag scales between 1 % and 1000 %. Each drag is one undo step, and a click
that doesn't move anything adds no step.

There is no separate anchor-point control. Rotation, the Picture tab's Scale

*Agents:* `paste_attributes`.

## Limits

- Scale is uniform for pictures. Only shapes (box width and height) and text
  (wrap width) can be stretched on one axis.
- At most four filters and four obscure regions per clip. Gradients have 2–8
  stops.
- Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key are only for video, image and still
  clips.
- A nest clip can't take a blend mode, and Add Blurred Background is not
  offered for one.
- **Eight clip buttons**: Split (⌘T), Trim Start to Playhead (W), Trim End
  to Playhead (E), Ripple Delete (⌘⌫), Add Marker (M), Duplicate (⌘D), Add
  Text (T) and Add Shape. Each button's tooltip names its key. **Add Shape**
  opens a menu of shapes and has no menu-bar item, so this button is the way
  to add one. What the edits do is on [Editing](editing.md); text and shapes

Settled from the code beyond the Swift and Rust sources:
- Font families and weights come from the bundled TTFs' name and fvar tables in app/Resources/Fonts, and all seven have OFL files.

Small imprecisions left as they are:
- Family order is Swift's sorted(), which is by Unicode, so a lowercase family name sorts after Z. The page says alphabetical.
- Past 8,192 px, an Auto-size line is cut by the texture cap. The page's next bullet already covers that limit.
- In and Out ramp inside an action only when the reveal kind is unchanged. A change of kind holds the whole reveal object until the action's end (core/src/actions.rs:264-270).
- The gradient's Stop rows carry no ⊘ of their own. The Gradient section's header shows ⊘ instead (app/Sources/InspectorMarks.swift, app/Sources/InspectorSection.swift).
